messages:
Maya: quick heads-up — putting this here so folks see it: after the kernel-selector tweak rolled into canary this morning, we're seeing ~2.2x p99 on host-side request path for short-chat workloads. flamegraph + traces uploaded.
BenchBot: perf-alert: host-p99 increased 2.1x for service=ingress-proxy on canary. threshold=1.5x.
Sam: ugh. which tweak exactly? the auto-kernel fallback patch?
Maya: yeah, the change that prefers the fused attention kernel for seq<128 when qkv type==fp16. landed at 05:12 UTC.
Li: can you paste the p99 numbers and a quick breakdown? is this CPU time during tokenization/parse or downstream GPU queueing?
Maya: quick breakdown from the flamegraph (host-side): tokenize ~5.8ms, preparse/route ~3.1ms, chunk-write/grpc ~4.2ms, kernel-selection overhead + syscall stalls ~2.6ms. total host contribution up ~9ms -> explains a lot for short requests. link: https://internal.artifacts/redwood/perf/7050002468/fg.html
Oliver: interesting that grpc chunking is 4.2ms. that matches the writev + tcp coalesce jitter we saw in 703xxx runs. are these single-chunk responses?
Maya: mostly single-chunk (<=1 payload write), small responses (<=64 tokens). batch-size=1 in the canary.
Jess: can we repro locally against the canary image? steps?
Maya: yes. sample harness:
```
wrk -t8 -c200 -d60s --latency "http://canary-ingress.local/generate?model=redwood-medium"
# payload: {"input":"short prompt"}
```
Also for gRPC streaming:
```
python tests/stream_ping.py --host canary-ingress.local --model redwood-medium --count 1000
```
Arjun: couple of hypotheses: 1) kernel-selector is adding a sync call to check kernel availability; 2) more frequent KV-cache misses due to slight change in routing leading to more expensive preparse; 3) smallwrites / writev path now hitting an extra header path.
Li: good list. I instrumented a canary request with `strace -f -tt -e write,read,ioctl` earlier — saw an extra ioctl on the fd before writev in ~60% of requests (timestamped). looks like the selector triggers a feature-check ioctl when fused kernel available.
Maya: exact log snippet from strace:
```
12:05:23.123456 ioctl(3, BIOC_KERN_CHECK, 0x7ffd1234) = 0
12:05:23.123459 writev(3, [{iov_base="...", iov_len=280}], 1) = 280
```
Sam: ioctl on the hotpath is bad. who added that check? we should cache the result per-process or per-worker.
Oliver: agreed. fastest mitigation: flip the selector to cache capability boolean in the worker init. Jess, could you try toggling `prefer_fused_attention` in canary config to false and re-run wrk?
Jess: on it. toggled via runtime flag: `--runtime.prefer_fused_attention=false` — re-running now
BenchBot: run complete. host-p99 down to baseline+5%. payload unchanged. summary: p99 improved from 2.2x -> 1.05x.
Jess: confirmed. flipping flag fixes it.
Arjun: so root cause = per-request capability probe. fix options: a) memoize probe per worker; b) move to init-time discovery; c) gate behind config so default is cached.
Li: also worth checking batching heuristic: selector was previously used inside the batch gather loop. if we move it to pre-batch decision we avoid per-request overhead.
Maya: Agreed. small public patch: move kernel-discovery to worker startup and remove ioctl from hotpath. I'll post a draft PR. quick patch diff:
```
- bool fused = probe_fused(); // called per-request
+ static thread_local bool fused_cached = probe_fused_at_startup();
+ bool fused = fused_cached;
```
Sam: also check KV cache metrics — I noticed a slight dip in kv_hit_rate coincident with the change. maybe some routing jitter. Maya, can you paste the `kv_hit_rate` time series?
Maya: screenshot uploaded. kv_hit_rate dropped from 98.6% -> 95.2% for a 10min window after deploy. seems correlated with a canary router config (round-robin weights changed).
Oliver: if routing moved traffic to less warmed hosts, that explains higher parse + chunking overhead too. two independent issues may have amplified.
Jess: action items: 1) revert per-request probe (hotfix) 2) memoize capability at worker init PR 3) investigate router weight change and warmup policy 4) add perf regression test for single-chunk short prompts.
Maya: I opened PR #3192 with the memoize change and smoke tests. putting canary back to stable until we merge.
Sam: +1. add a small unit test asserting no ioctl in fastpath (use LD_PRELOAD stub or mock).
Arjun: also add a metric `host.kernel_probe_calls` we can alert on. if it spikes, it indicates regression.
Maya: will add metric and dashboard.
BenchBot: ticket created: PERF-1221 "Fix per-request kernel probe causing host p99 regression" assigned to Maya.
Oliver: nice find. thanks everyone. we should also add a note in release notes to avoid similar hotpath probes. :memo:
Maya: thanks — I'll follow up with the core runtime folks to add a linter rule for syscalls on the request path.
